title: Is the world going to end in 2012?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the 2012 doomsday phenomenon, prompted by a listener suggestion from Jason of Santa Barbara. They open with a near-miss asteroid passing about 50,000 miles from Earth, then cover the December 21, 2012 end-date theory based on the Mayan Long Count calendar (the end of the 5,125-year Great Cycle, the winter solstice, 11:11 a.m. Greenwich Mean Time). They discuss Mayan achievements in mathematics and zero, calendars, and how the Mayans themselves did not predict an apocalypse. They cover the Y2K comparison, eco and climate-change anxieties, and astronomical claims (sun in line with Milky Way center, a new sunspot cycle, and magnetic pole reversal). They conclude that mainstream scientists dismiss the prophecy and that the world probably won't end in 2012. The episode ends with plugs for the Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy spoken-word album, the blog, and the retirement of the Haiku Theater listener-mail segment.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and near-miss asteroid
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, joking about the 2012 movie and Michael Bay. They discuss a recent asteroid passing about 50,000 miles from Earth, which NASA considers a close call, and comparison to the Siberian impact.

segments.title: Introducing the December 2012 doomsday date
segments.summary: Chuck introduces listener Jason's suggestion about 2012 doomsday theories. The specific date is December 21, 2012, the winter solstice, with a stated moment of 11:11 a.m. Greenwich Mean Time. Patrick of Belgium is cited as a leader of a group preparing a refuge in Africa.

segments.title: Y2K comparison and eco-anxiety
segments.summary: The hosts compare the 2012 fears to Y2K anxiety, noting that cultural concerns drive doomsday prophecies. They tie the 2012 movement to green consciousness and global warming fears, and note that the scientific picture is uncertain.

segments.title: Mayan calendars and the Long Count
segments.summary: The hosts describe Mayan achievements in writing, astronomy, mathematics including zero, and architecture. They explain the Tzolkin, Haab, Calendar Round, and Long Count calendars, and how scholars correlated the Long Count with the Gregorian calendar to arrive at December 2012 as the end of the Great Cycle.

segments.title: Mayans did not predict the end of the world
segments.summary: The hosts note that the Mayans viewed the date as the start of a new Great Cycle, not an apocalypse, and that Mayan scholars are upset about the misrepresentation. The conquistadors' destruction of Mayan culture is mentioned as the source of the lost record.

segments.title: Astronomical claims: galactic alignment, sunspots, pole reversal
segments.summary: Chuck describes claims that the sun will be at the center of the Milky Way on the winter solstice, a rare event, and that a new sunspot cycle began with a backwards sunspot seen by NASA in 2006. They also discuss the Earth's magnetic field reversal, which lava-flow evidence shows happens roughly every 780,000 years. The hosts say most scientists dismiss these claims.

segments.title: Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy plug and blog
segments.summary: Hosts promote the Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy spoken-word album on iTunes and the show's blog.

segments.title: Haiku Theater retirement and final haiku
segments.summary: The hosts retire the Haiku Theater segment and read a few final listener haiku, including one from Austin of Fort Worth, Texas. They sign off with an email address for listener contact.
